title: Closed-point Picard classes lift across compactification
statement: Let C be a smooth affine connected curve over an algebraically closed field k [def-sc-curves], c its smooth connected compactification [lem-sc-compactification], and Q a closed point of C. Its image is a closed point P of c.Z, and pullback on Picard groups [def-sc-picard-group] sends the class O(P) to O(Q). Here both classes are the duals of the reduced point ideals [def-sc-invertible-module].

source.place: Proof: first paragraph, restriction and boundary divisors

proof.text: Use the rational point x associated to Q. Its composite with c.i is a section of the separated morphism c.g, hence a closed immersion. Its topological image is the singleton c.i(Q), proving closedness of P. This is implemented using pointOfClosedPoint, pointOfClosedPoint_comp, pointOfClosedPoint_apply and isClosedImmersion_of_comp_eq_id.

Set I and J to the reduced point ideals of Q and P. The theorem IdealSheafData.map_vanishingIdeal identifies I.map c.i with J; the already proved source theorem IdealSheafData.comap_map gives J.comap c.i = I because c.i is a quasi-compact flat monomorphism. Quasi-compactness follows from C being Noetherian. Both ideals are invertible by the closed-point Cartier theorem.

Apply the source nonempty_pullback_dual_toModules_iso to J and its invertible comap. Compose with the comap equality and the Picard representative isomorphisms. Pic.eq_iff_nonempty_iso then gives the displayed equality. This is the pointwise use of the existing effective-Cartier pullback comparison.

lean.statement:
theorem Scheme.Hom.pic_restriction_point_lift
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {C : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsConnectedCurve f] [Smooth f] [IsAffine C]
    (c : Compactification f) [IsConnectedCurve c.g]
    [hsm : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 c.g] [hC : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f]
    (Q : closedPoints C) :
    ∃ P : closedPoints c.Z, P.val = c.i.base Q.val ∧
      Scheme.Pic.mapHom c.i (@Scheme.Pic.ofClosedPoint k _ c.Z ⟨c.g⟩ hsm P) =
        @Scheme.Pic.ofClosedPoint k _ C ⟨f⟩ hC Q
